changes.narration: This approach colors each sampled point by its output quadrant relative to a chosen origin. Greater rendering resolution reveals finer boundaries. Colors indicate direction; at a zero, the phase is undefined.

bulletReplacements.text: Resolution refines sampling; it does not certify a boundary.

interpretativeNote: This is one chosen origin in the output plane, with one quadrant color assigned to each nonzero input sample. It does not assert independent self-solving axes at every point. Greater sampling resolution can expose finer rendered structure; it does not certify an exact boundary or exclude unresolved features. At zero, phase remains undefined.

drawOrderNote.currentMeaning: The current phase grid first computes the mathematical quadrant at each sample. When separately rendered strokes overlap, draw order or blending determines the visible pixel; that compositing outcome is not a mathematical proof or an additional quadrant invariant.
drawOrderNote.proposedControl: A future forward-versus-reversed draw-order comparison could identify rendering artifacts while holding sample coordinates and computed quadrant values fixed. This control has not been implemented in the present deliverable.
